what: Radiance cascades (web/shaders/cascades): GPU passes (f32) against the float64 CPU reference, cascades and brute force
why: Both sides run the same steps in the same order; f32 against f64 moves chord lengths and angles by rounding, and a ray flips only where it grazes a pixel corner or a circle tangent. Relative RMSE is over every channel of every pixel, divided by the f64 side's mean.
amended: 2026-11-06, after the first runs on the RTX 4090. Run 1 failed glass-b4 cascades (1.4e-2) and both glass reference cases (4.3e-2): WGSL sin, cos and atan2 carry loose accuracy bounds (sin and cos 2^-11 absolute), enough to move a bent ray a quarter of a fine cascade's bin. The fix (angles reduced to [-pi, pi], atan2 refined by one Newton step) brought glass-b4 to 9.3e-6. The glass reference still differs by 7.7e-2 relative RMSE at 64 rays: 15 of 576 samples differ by more than 0.05 and the rest agree. The glass circle focuses a small bright emitter, so a direction change of f32 rounding size turns a ray from missing the emitter to hitting it (the same flips appear on the CPU when the circle moves 3e-5 px: 2.8e-2). The glass reference is therefore bounded by the fraction of samples that differ by more than 1e-3 relative (glass_reference_flip_fraction), and its relative RMSE is reported, not bounded. Every other bound is unchanged.
